title: Wring a wet sponge into a basin and return it to its rack
instruction: Hold both ends of the wet sponge over the basin and wring water into it. Return the sponge to the rack.
context: A wet cleaning sponge is wrung before storage. The arms need opposing grips on a flexible body while keeping the runoff inside the basin.
setup: A 152 by 91 by 24 mm cellulose sponge holds 90 g of water across rack bars at X 448, Y 0 mm. A 198 by 284 mm basin sits at X 295, Y 0 mm. Both are inside a lined 368 by 402 mm catch tray with clear 64 mm high sides. Fit both grippers with thin waterproof boots with textured pads before a physical wet trial.
scoring: Weigh the basin and all outside catch surfaces separately. Score 0 for above 5 g spilled outside the basin or below 20 g caught. Score 0.25 at 20 g caught and 0.5 at 40 g. Score 1.0 if at least 40 g are caught, at most 5 g are spilled and the sponge is released on its rack.
reset_notes: Restore the sponge to its dry reference mass plus 90 g of water. Empty the basin, replace and tare the catch liners and inspect that both waterproof boots are intact and dry inside before replacing the sponge.
fidelity: Native joints transmit twist resistance between physically grasped sections. Collision geometry represents the splash panels. The simulator estimates water transfer with stock gripper contact shapes. The waterproof boots require the fit, grip and leak checks in the README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; stock YAM scripted demo: 1.0
